title: SLO Decision Simulator and Incident Evidence Procedure
author: Marcus Nguyen
Content:
SUMMARY
This runbook describes a structured, simulation-driven process for making SLO and error-budget decisions during service incidents, combined with a standardized incident evidence collection procedure for SRE oncall. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during high-severity events, preserve forensic-quality evidence for postmortems, and produce repeatable capacity-recovery actions (eviction, throttles, headroom grants) evaluated by a decision simulator before execution.

SCOPE
- Applies to Redwood multi-tenant inference services (model serving, routing, cache, admission)
- Intended for SRE oncall, incident commanders (ICs), and service owners
- Covers: realtime simulation of SLO outcomes, pre-validated capacity recovery playbooks, and evidence packaging for incident review

BACKGROUND
SLO breaches are often the consequence of complex interactions between demand surges, quantization-induced tail latency, and cold KV-cache misses. Prior incidents revealed two persistent failure modes:
1) ad-hoc throttle/eviction decisions that increase blast radius
2) incomplete telemetry/evidence causing ambiguous postmortem conclusions

This runbook introduces a lightweight decision simulator that runs candidate mitigations against a short-window replay of telemetry and a defined tenant-impact model, producing expected SLO trajectories and error-budget burn estimate. The simulator is intended to be fast (<= 60s) and conservative.

DEFINITIONS
- SLO: Service Level Objective (see SLO catalog for thresholds)
- Error budget: remaining allowed SLO violation percentage for the assessment window
- Decision simulator: a deterministic emulator that replays recent telemetry and computes the projected effect of mitigation actions
- Evidence bundle: time-bounded set of telemetry and artifacts stored for post-incident analysis

PREREQUISITES
- Access to incident-simulator CLI (inc-sim) and playbook runner (play-run)
- Permissions to create evidence bundles (GCS bucket: gs://redwood-incident-evidence)
- Slack channel and PagerDuty escalation path for the affected service

SIMULATOR OVERVIEW
The decision simulator accepts three inputs:
1) telemetry window (T0..Tn, default 15m)
2) mitigation candidate (e.g., "evict-tenant X", "apply-throttle 20%", "add-burst-pool +10%)")
3) tenant impact model (fairshare or committed)

Output:
- projected 99th/95th latency quantiles over next 30m
- projected error-budget burn rate
- risk score (0–10) capturing blast-radius and customer-impact

RUNBOOK: DURING AN INCIDENT (Triage → Simulation → Action)
1) Initial triage (0–5m)
   - Confirm service impact on status page and channels
   - Identify affected routes and tenants using "slo-query --service <svc> --window 15m"
   - Tag incident severity: Sev1 if >25% customers impacted or >2x SLO burn rate
2) Evidence snapshot (first 5m)
   - Run: 
     ```
     inc-sim snapshot --service <svc> --window 15m --out /tmp/evidence-<ts>.tgz
     gsutil cp /tmp/evidence-<ts>.tgz gs://redwood-incident-evidence/<svc>/<ts>/
     ```
   - Ensure the following are captured in the snapshot:
     - request traces (sampled traces spanning window)
     - token-level tail latency histogram
     - admission and queue lengths
     - current cache hit rates and warm pool sizes
     - autoscaler events and recent scaling history
3) Run Decision Simulator (5–10m)
   - For each mitigation candidate, run:
     ```
     inc-sim run --evidence gs://redwood-incident-evidence/<svc>/<ts>/ --mitigation "evict-tenant T123" --model fairshare --timeout 60
     ```
   - Compare outputs and sort by risk score and projected error-budget savings
   - Document the selected mitigation and why it was chosen in the incident timeline
4) Execute low-risk mitigations (10–30m)
   - If simulator projects >50% reduction in 99th latency and risk score <=3, proceed with automated play-run
     ```
     play-run execute --play evict-tenant --tenant T123 --dry-run=false
     ```
   - If mitigation is higher risk (score 4–7), perform a canary: apply to single cluster or 10% traffic lane
   - If simulator projects high blast risk (score >7), do not execute; instead escalate to oncall lead
5) Verify and iterate (30–60m)
   - After mitigation, collect second snapshot and re-run inc-sim to ensure trajectory improved
   - If not improved, consult escalation matrix

EVIDENCE COLLECTION CHECKLIST (MANDATORY)
- Snapshot archive: telemetry (traces, histograms), autoscaler logs, admission logs (size <= 1GB recommended)
- Request sample set: 1000 requests representative across tenants/routes
- Config diffs: model versions active, routing policy changes, config pushes in last 24h
- Play-run audit: who executed playbook, run output and timestamps
- Preservation: copy bundle to gs://redwood-incident-evidence/<svc>/<incident-id>/preserved and mark immutable

EVIDENCE RETENTION POLICY
- Active incident bundle: retained for 90 days with full fidelity
- Preserved evidence for postmortem: retained for 2 years (encrypted at rest, access audited)
- Trimmed anonymized snapshot for long-term analytics: retained indefinitely (PII removed)

POST-INCIDENT: SIMULATION-BASED REMEDIATION AND CAPACITY RECOVERY
- Within 24 hours of mitigation, run an expanded simulation for 7-day demand scenarios to recommend permanent changes:
  - headroom pool sizing
  - burst credit policy
  - tenant isolation thresholds
- Recommended artifacts for the remediation PR:
  - simulator config used and seed telemetry
  - capacity-sizing table (see example below)
  - rollback criteria and monitoring alerts

Example capacity-sizing table (to include in remediation PR):
| Metric | Current | Simulated 95th | Recommend |
|--------|---------|----------------|-----------|
| GPU count | 120 | 140 | 140 |
| Warm-pool size | 30 | 40 | 40 |
| Admission throttle (%) | 0 | 15 | 10 |
| Estimated cost delta | $0 | +$8,400/mo | +$8,400/mo |

INCIDENT REVIEW STANDARD (EVIDENCE & ACTION VERIFICATION)
- Required data for postmortem acceptance:
  1) Immutable evidence bundle link
  2) Simulator runs and versions used (inc-sim hash)
  3) Chronological action list with timestamps and play-run outputs
  4) Customer impact classification and credits issuance plan (if applicable)
- Postmortem should include a simulation replay: run inc-sim with preserved bundle and publish results in the PR

OPERATIONAL TOOLING INTEGRATION
- inc-sim: decision simulator (internal binary), runs locally or on CI; logs JSON results to stdout and GCS
- play-run: standardized playbook executor with audit logging and dry-run support
- evidence-orch: microservice that enforces retention and immutability policies
- Dashboards:
  - /dashboards/slo-decision-simulator (live simulator health and queue)
  - /dashboards/incident-evidence (most recent preserved bundles across services)

ESCALATION & OWNERSHIP
- Incident Commander (IC): executes simulation and authorizes low-risk mitigations
- Oncall Lead: required approval for high-risk mitigations (risk score >7)
- Service Owner: owns remediation PR and capacity changes
- Evidence Steward (rotating): ensures evidence bundles are preserved and accessible within 30 minutes of incident resolution

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (quick reference)
- SRE Oncall: run inc-sim, create snapshot, execute play-run for low-risk mitigations
- Oncall Lead: approve high-risk actions and coordinate customer comms
- Platform Security: review preserved evidence access requests for restricted incidents

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATE (Slack + Post-incident)
- Slack snippet to post after mitigation:
  "Mitigation applied: evict-tenant T123 at 2027-02-08T14:23Z. Simulator projected 99th latency drop from 380ms → 150ms. Evidence bundle: gs://redwood-incident-evidence/model-serving/20270208-1423/preserved.tar.gz"

APPENDIX: QUICK COMMANDS
- Create snapshot and upload:
  ```
  inc-sim snapshot --service model-serving --window 15m --out /tmp/evidence.tgz && gsutil cp /tmp/evidence.tgz gs://redwood-incident-evidence/model-serving/<ts>/
  ```
- Run simulator locally:
  ```
  inc-sim run --evidence gs://... --mitigation "apply-throttle 10%" --timeout 30
  ```
- Execute playbook (with audit):
  ```
  play-run execute --play apply-throttle --service model-serving --percent 10
  ```

APPROVALS AND REVIEW CYCLE
- This document should be reviewed quarterly by SRE reliability leads and product service owners. Simulator models must be versioned and validated twice per quarter against synthetic load tests.
